verdict_reason: The shipped quantity -- mean over tokens of ||h_{l+1}-h_l|| / ||h_l||, aggregated over adjacent layer pairs -- is computed correctly on every reachable input. Against an independent float64 recomputation on real gpt2 the worst per-pair relative error is 7.294e-09, and the ratio's defining scale invariance holds exactly across the whole ladder: relative_change_mean reads 1.320529725 / 1.320529726 / 1.320529722 / 1.320529724 / 1.320529728 / 1.320529724 / 1.320529723 / 1.320529723 at 1e-30 through 6.656e17, with contractive_fraction pinned at 0.833333 throughout. The class docstring is honest that this is a relative-change ratio, not the operator Lipschitz constant.
comparable_reason: relative_change_mean falls with depth within every family measured: distilgpt2 (L=6) 2.22800 vs gpt2 (L=12) 1.32053, and pythia-70m (L=6) 6.98364 vs pythia-160m (L=12) 2.54460 -- a 1.7x to 2.7x drop from doubling depth alone. contractive_fraction moves the same way (0.6667 / 0.8333 for the GPT pair, 0.3333 / 0.7500 for the pythia pair). relative_change_max is worse still: in 3 of the 4 models it is the embedding -> block-0 transition (pair 0: 9.68591 / 11.12356 / 16.07173), so the headline maximum is measuring the embedding-to-residual-stream jump rather than any block.
github_reason: No code was ever released for this quantity, and none exists to release: it is a BLME-defined layer-transition ratio, not a published estimator. The class docstring says so explicitly ('sometimes called empirical Lipschitz constant, but it measures ... rather than the true operator Lipschitz constant'). I therefore verified against an independent float64 recomputation (7.294e-09) rather than a reference implementation. Recording NONE is the honest answer here.
paper_reason: There is no source paper publishing a value for mean per-token relative residual change on a named checkpoint, so nothing to reproduce. The manuscript's own requested output, contractive_fraction, IS present and I verified it on the analytic anchor: layer means [0.5, 2.0] give exactly 0.500000.
confounds_reason: Depth, within family and across: mean relative change 2.22800 -> 1.32053 for GPT L=6 -> 12 and 6.98364 -> 2.54460 for pythia L=6 -> 12. This is structural -- a deeper model spreads the same total representational change over more transitions, so the per-transition mean falls roughly as 1/L. d_model does not enter (the ratio is dimensionless and I measured it invariant under uniform rescaling to 1e-9); vocabulary does not enter at all.
defects: CODE, EXTREME-SCALE, REACHABILITY 1.11e35x: lipschitz.py:150 computes h_next - h_l in float32 BEFORE _rownorm promotes at :44, so a near-sign-flip at the top of the float32 range overflows and the pair is reported NaN. Reproduced: the one-coordinate trajectory [s, -s, -s] at s=2.406159650500376e38 -- every stored value finite -- gives layer means [nan, 0.0] instead of the exact [2, 0], and contractive_fraction 1.0000 instead of 0.5. A UNIFORM scale-up of real gpt2 states stays correct all the way to 3.4028e38, the entire float32 range; the failure additionally requires the near-antipodal update. gpt2's largest hidden coordinate is 3054.12. The same one-line ordering issue exists in geometry_effective_depth, and there the released Csordas reference has it too.

COMPARABILITY: relative_change_mean is a ~1/L depth proxy (1.7-2.7x from L=6 to L=12 within family), and relative_change_max is the embedding -> block-0 jump in 3 of 4 models rather than a block transition.

ROBUSTNESS, OUT OF DOMAIN: _rownorm([[nan, 3]]) returns 0.0, because the nz mask is m > 0 and NaN > 0 is False. A NaN row therefore reads as a zero row and is excluded by the input_norms > 0 filter rather than flagged, so a partially corrupt checkpoint yields a plausible number with no count emitted. Contrast intrinsic_dim and hubness, which both count non-finite rows into _meta_ keys.

PROTOCOL (not implementation, and not re-filed): the epsilon-free headline diverges from the manuscript's 1e-8-clamped denominator by design; the paper form is emitted separately as _meta_relative_change_mean_paper_eps, which is documented at lipschitz.py:270-283.
fix: Promote before subtracting, both loops: lipschitz.py:150-151 and :198-199 should do np.asarray(..., dtype=np.float64) on h_l and h_next before h_next - h_l, exactly as _rownorm does internally one line later. Separately, make _rownorm's nz mask distinguish NaN from zero (np.isfinite(m) & (m > 0)) and count the excluded rows into a _meta_ key.
